page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a 32-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the arm64 architecture, this server allocates 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, which positions it as a compute-focused, low-memory configuration. The instance includes 1890 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory throughput. The server achieved a top-tier rating in large-block read memory bandwidth at 450.77 GB/sec and a strong rating in write bandwidth at 169.21 GB/sec. Multi-core processing capabilities are highlighted by a strong stress-ng multi-core score of 66296.43 and a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 19774.0. Database and web serving capabilities are also notable, with Passmark database operations scoring in the top tier at 37222.49 and static web serving throughput reaching a strong 53.68 GB/sec. However, large-scale AI workloads show limitations, as LLM inference for a 70B model yielded a poor prompt processing speed of 4.66 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Neoverse-N2 architecture provides high resource density and compute performance per unit of power, making it an efficient option for scale-out workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The combination of dedicated physical cores, high memory bandwidth, and 1890 GB of local storage makes this server well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, Redis caching, and high-throughput static web serving. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM parameter inference.
